title: Pens: enclosure, access and a food budget
applies_when: A pen alert or animal housing objective needs assessment, before approving construction.
approach: Containment and feeding are separate requirements. A pen-needed alert does not establish a suitable pasture. Before approving a site, identify edible vegetation and seasonal regrowth, or an available feed source plus reachable feed storage/delivery. Bare sand can contain an animal but must not be counted as grazing nutrition. Unknown feed capacity is an inspection dependency, not proof the pen will support the animal.
A pen requires a closed barrier, a usable gate or door, and a pen marker. An ordinary painted zone is not a pen.
Size pasture against observed animal consumption and pen nutrition, not a fixed tile count. Vegetation, season and regrowth matter; bare land can provide little feed even in a large pen.
Keep human crops and hay intended for harvesting outside grazing access. Reserve a route for handling and feed delivery, and room for herd growth.
Keep grazing outdoors. An animal flap can connect a sheltered sleeping area; prepare stored suitable feed for cold seasons when grazing fails.

For supplied feeding, grow haygrass outside grazing access and harvest it; animals eating growing haygrass lose the larger harvested yield. Specify separate growing/storage work only when needed and affordable, continuing existing food/feed projects rather than duplicating them. Do not mark the animal housing goal achieved merely because a marker or fence exists.
verify: Native pen recognition and access; the animal can reach edible pasture or delivered feed; available nutrition and replenishment cover observed consumption. A completed enclosure alone is not a sustainable pen.
reconsider: Animals outgrow the food budget, pasture loses vegetation or winter approaches.
